title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 15
paragraphs: On the third day the barbarian commanders, exceedingly indignant that so small a number of ships should do them such damage, and fearing what Xerxes might do, this time did not wait for the Greeks to begin the fight but passed the word of command and launched their ships around midday. Now it so happened that these battles at sea and the battles on land at Thermopylae took place on the same days. For those fighting at sea, the whole aim of the contest concerned the Euripos channel, just as the aim of Leonidas and his men was to guard the pass. So the Greeks exhorted one another not to let the barbarians pass into Greece, while the barbarians urged each other on to destroy the Greek fleet and gain possession of the straits.
